transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-28
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Li (Redwood CSM), Ava Torres (VP Product, Elysium), Markus Voss (Head of ML Ops), Priya Nair (Infrastructure Lead)

---
Summary (auto): QBR focused on usage growth (x2 q/q), cost drivers (long-context chat, embeddings), reliability incidents in Feb (fallbacks to smaller model), and customer interest in Dedicated reserved capacity. Action items captured.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, i'm joined by ravi and jordan. how's everyone doing?
[00:07] Ava: good thanks, ava here. excited to go through the QBR.
[00:10] Markus: hi, markus, quick heads up we're on a slightly delayed release today so if i seem distracted that's why.
[00:15] Jordan: totally fine, we can run through the slides fast.
[02:02] Maya: okay quick agenda, usage and cost trends, reliability incidents and root causes, dedicated pilot discussion, security and roadmap, then next steps.
[02:20] Markus: sounds good.
[03:12] Maya: first up usage — we see you've doubled monthly token volume since december, most growth is from your customer support chat and the batch reranking job in europe region. long context sessions (4k+ tokens) are the largest per-token cost driver, plus embeddings during nightly re-indexing. is that consistent with what you see?
[03:37] Priya: yes that's accurate. we also started a pilot in APAC which added about 12% to traffic and we saw some cost bump.
[03:45] Ravi: just to add, on the infra side we noticed more KV cache misses with the new session affinity config, that increased per-request compute.
[03:58] Ava: KV cache misses, is that something we can tune? we've been seeing a weird latency tail.
[04:04] Ravi: yes, we're recommending a prefix caching policy and a slightly longer TTL for session cache, that usually cuts token cost by ~8-12% for chat workloads. i'll share configs.
[04:15] Ava: cool.
[05:30] Maya: costs — your effective per-1k token rate is up due to model mix; you're running a mix of redwood-2-large and a smaller fallback. the fallbacks happened more in feb during our incident window.
[05:45] Markus: can you remind me of the fallbacks? i thought fallback is automatic when capacity is low. what was the trigger?
[06:00] Jordan: quick recap: feb 18th we had a partial region degradation, smart routing started falling back to a smaller model variant to keep latency SLO. that preserved availability but affected quality for some enterprise users.
[06:15] Markus: right, we logged a couple customer complaints about hallucination in support answers.
[06:22] Maya: yep, and that's why many customers ask for Dedicated reserved capacity to avoid noisy neighbors and automatic fallbacks.
[06:30] Ava: that's actually our concern — predictable quality is more important than a few percentage points of cost savings.
[06:37] Maya: understood. Dedicated gives you pinned capacity and SLA-backed latency. we'll size for your peak qps and plan a canary rollout.
[07:05] Ravi: from the SE perspective, the main engineering tasks are model pinning, autoscale thresholds, and setting up capacity buffers for bursts. also we need to tune batching parameters so you don't increase latency.
[08:00] Priya: on security, we need SOC2 evidence and details on audit logs retention, SSO and KMS integration. what's included for Dedicated/Private?
[08:14] Jordan: for Dedicated the control plane is managed and we provide audit logs, RBAC, and KMS integrations; for Private deploy we can offer customer-managed networking and HSM/KMS integration. i'll send the SOC2 pack and architecture notes.
[08:35] Priya: perfect, please include data residency options because our compliance team will want that.
[09:00] Maya: noted.
[09:45] Ava: timeline-wise, we want a pilot in q2 and a production cutover by q3, ideally. is that realistic?
[09:58] Maya: yes a 3-month pilot on Dedicated is typical: first two weeks for onboarding and benchmarking, then 2 months of evaluation. we can target pilot start mid-April.
[10:10] Markus: for benchmarks, can you measure p95/p99 latency, tail latencies during burst, cost delta vs hosted, and quality regression tests against our prompt set?
[10:24] Ravi: absolutely — we'll run scripted load tests and evaluate on your evaluation harness. we should sync on the prompt set and acceptance criteria.
[10:40] Ava: acceptance criteria: p95 < 200ms, p99 < 600ms for standard chat, no more than 2% quality regression on our top-50 prompts.
[10:50] Maya: got it, we'll confirm exact numbers in the pilot doc.
[11:30] Jordan: reliability note — regarding the feb incident, devops traced the region failure to a networking misconfiguration in the cloud provider; smart routing responded but default policy allowed fallbacks to smaller model which increased errors. we recommended a fallback policy change: maintain quality-first for enterprise routes.
[12:05] Markus: can that be applied only to our enterprise route? we don't want it globally changed.
[12:12] Ravi: yes routing policies are per-route, we can pin enterprise route to a quality-first policy and route non-critical traffic to cheaper variants.
[12:25] Priya: good.
[13:10] Maya: roadmap — upcoming features: additional telemetry (token-level cost breakdown per route), faster warm KV cache warmup for long-context sessions, and tighter RBAC on dedicated deployments. rollout for the telemetry is planned late q2.
[13:35] Ava: the token-level breakdown will be useful for our finance team.
[13:40] Maya: we'll give you access to the per-route dashboard and we'll export a monthly CSV for your cost center reconciliation.
[14:00] Markus: one more technical ask: we may need on-prem for a subset of sensitive customers. what's the path to private deployment?
[14:12] Jordan: private is available; it requires a separate license and planning for network, secrets, and ops. timeline is typically 8-12 weeks from start. for now Dedicated looks like the right first step.
[14:30] Ava: agreed.
[20:05] Ravi: small engineering note — your nightly embedding re-index spikes cause transient GPU contention. we recommend either staggered jobs or moving to a quantized model for embeddings to drop memory and cost. quantizing embeddings model gives you 2-3x memory reduction but we should validate quality.
[20:30] Priya: we can try staggered jobs first. please provide a config sample.
[21:00] Maya: action recap — we will send pilot proposal and pricing, ravi will share benchmark plan and config samples, jordan will send SOC2 and architecture docs, and priya will share compliance list.
[30:12] Ava: thanks, that's great. one question — competitors: we evaluated Anthropic and one of the cloud managed endpoint offerings, how do you compare on unit economics?
[30:30] Maya: high level, Redwood's strengths are in serving latency and cost controls via batching, kv cache, and quantization suggestions plus unified routing across regions. we'll include a simple competitive summary in the follow-up.
[31:05] Markus: can you also include expected uplift in p95/p99 if we move to Dedicated? numbers help justify the spend.
[31:15] Maya: yes we'll include estimated p95/p99 improvements from prior pilots.
[40:00] Jordan: any other questions?
[40:12] Priya: one small ask: audit log retention beyond 12 months, possible?
[40:18] Maya: yes for enterprise we support extended retention as an add-on. we'll include pricing.
[45:50] Ava: ok i'm happy with next steps.
[46:04] Maya: great, thanks everyone; we'll follow up with the pilot doc and schedule the onboarding call for week of april 12th.
[46:22] Markus: thanks all.
[46:30] Meeting end

---
